scenarios.description: The five-minute-quickstart deterministic campaign (docs/five-minute-quickstart.md), driven through the compiled production CLI entry instead of bin/arbor-mcp.mjs's esbuild bundle. CORRECTED 2026-08-20: an earlier version of this description claimed this scenario "drives createProductionCampaignRunner through the arbor-opencode loop" — verified false by reading cli.ts. `arbor run`/`arbor demo` (args[0] === "run"||"demo") dispatches straight to demo.ts's own `demomain`, which composes its own `WorktreeManager` and `createDemoConfig`/`runOneCampaign` and never calls `createCliRuntime`. `createProductionCampaignRunner` (cli.ts:607) is constructed only inside `createCliRuntime` (cli.ts:1169) and reached from `serve`/`webui`/`task`/`report`/`recover`/`debug prompt-input`/`project *` — confirmed empirically: its observations in this store come from production-mcp-approval-agent-dispatch, production-mcp-evidence-surface-dispatch, production-recover-preview-unknown-campaign and production-tui-headless-boot, never from this one. What this scenario actually does, absent worktree isolation (no real git repo in its scratch cwd — see production-git-repo-real-agent-loop-campaign for the git_init variant that clears that gate): exercises demo.ts's deterministic executor end to end up to the isolation-gate rejection on every one of the 8 demo-plan nodes (critic_agent: "loop").
Cheap coverage of the top-level argument dispatcher and usage text.

ledger verify against a fresh temp dir with no campaign yet written. Exit 3 (PARTIAL) is the real, verified behavior: the ledger loader reports the campaign as intact but with tip_status sentinel_missing, not an error — verified empirically 2026-08-11 against packages/arbor-mcp/dist/cli.js.
Native harness readiness inspection without probing providers or reading credentials — exercises config composition and readiness-assessment code paths.

arbor project status against the scenario's own empty scratch cwd, which is never an enrolled project. Exit 4 is the real, verified behavior (state 'not_enrolled', six repairable findings) — verified empirically 2026-08-18, stable over three runs. Drives the project-lifecycle status path, which no prior scenario reached: the multi-project surface was entirely unobserved, so gate-relevant symbols in project-registry.ts and project-lifecycle.ts read as never-invoked.

arbor project enroll --new into the scenario's own scratch cwd. Hermetic and verified non-leaking: it writes the overlay, policy config, decisions/ and AGENTS.md into the temp dir only, and does NOT touch this repository's .arbor/project-registry.json (checked by hash before and after, three runs). Registration is then correctly REFUSED because a fresh temp dir has no resolvable git revision — so this scenario also covers the discharge-refusal path, not just the happy path. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-18.

arbor project registry list --json. Drives the registry read path (readSharedReservations and the registry loader) from a cwd holding no registry. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-18, stable over three runs.

arbor project registry verify --json. Drives verifyRegistryEntry and the discharge check — the half of the registry surface that list does not reach. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-18, stable over three runs.

arbor project manage --json, the one-pass reconciliation across enrolled projects. Over an empty registry it reconciles nothing and exits 0 — verified empirically 2026-08-18, stable over three runs. Included because manage is the entry point operators are pointed at, and it was wholly unobserved.

arbor project repair --apply against the scenario's own empty scratch cwd, which materialises the overlay and arbor.jsonc there. Added deliberately to close a hollow_candidate the FIRST catalog widening had just surfaced: repairProjectOverlay was production-reachable, tested and instrument-visible but invoked by nothing in the catalog. Hermetic and verified non-leaking — it writes only into the temp cwd and leaves this repository's .arbor/project-registry.json byte-identical (hash checked before and after, three runs). Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-18, stable over three runs.

arbor tui --renderer stdout against the scenario's own empty scratch cwd, with stdin closed immediately (vi-observe's default: no `input` given still yields an EOF'd child stdin, verified empirically against a minimal fixture). The TUI's own `stdin.once("end", finish)` shutdown path turns that EOF into a clean exit — no --renderer opentui native dependency, no real terminal, no timing race. Drives the full boot sequence for real: createCliRuntime, RuntimeCatalogRouter, RuntimePortAdapter, HeadlessHarness (@arbor/tui), installScreens, TuiShell.start(), the initial campaign.list/dashboard/cockpit/projects product-surface queries, and StdoutRenderer's frame draw and restore() on shutdown. This is the ONLY scenario in the catalog that loads packages/arbor-tui at all — every prior scenario left it at zero invocations regardless of reachability or test coverage. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-19 (real invocation, three runs, stable), confirmed to produce non-empty NODE_V8_COVERAGE for a packages/arbor-tui/dist/*.js file. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same TUI background-timer wall-clock race as production-tui-resume-execution-status-poll (verified empirically 2026-09-18: widgets.ts render-path symbols isCombining/isWide/width vary run to run even though this scenario supplies static stdin with no stdin_linger_ms -- the race is inherent to spawning the TUI's several independent setInterval timers at all, not specific to the linger mechanism). See vi-observe.mjs's count_semantics handling.

arbor recover --campaign <unknown> --json against the scenario's own empty scratch cwd. Drives runRecoveryCommand -> RecoveryService.previewContinuation over a real ArborRuntime with no interruption journal to find, returning {ok:true, authorized:false, plans:[]}. Genuinely exercises the crash-continuation preview path (recovery/recovery-command.ts, the recoveryService lookup, resumableReviewNodes' try/catch) rather than fabricating an interrupted-session fixture by hand — no prior scenario reached this module at all. A true mid-run SIGTERM-and-resume scenario was investigated and rejected: producing one deterministically would require either racing a real child process's timing (non-hermetic) or hand-writing an internal interruption-journal record (testing internals, not the real surface); this scenario is the honest, real-surface subset of that path. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-19, stable over three runs. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same /proc-walking sandbox admission read as cli-serve-junior-tier-denied-mutation's note, verified empirically 2026-09-18.

arbor governance --json, the governance projection subcommand named as unobserved dispatch surface. Needs a decisions/ directory to exist under the scratch cwd (its absence is a real, verified exit 1 — ENOENT reading the decisions directory — confirmed empirically 2026-08-19; seeding an empty one is the minimal hermetic fixture that reaches the real success path instead). Drives buildGovernanceSnapshot, the legacy-decision classifier, policy-findings evaluation, and governance-event witnessing/ledger save, none of which any prior scenario reached. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-19, stable over three runs.

arbor project registry list --json against a scratch cwd pre-seeded with one real-shaped project-registry.json entry (schema_version 1, all six required ProjectRegistryEntry fields). Every prior registry scenario ran against an EMPTY registry (the read-nothing path); this is the populated read path — loadProjectRegistry's entry-shape validation and formatRegistryList's non-empty formatting, neither reached before. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-19, stable over three runs.

arbor project registry verify --json against the same seeded registry entry, whose path (/nonexistent/vi-observe-fixture-project) does not exist and whose expires date (2020-01-01) is already past. This is the fault/error-injection scenario: evaluateProjectRegistry's real discharge check runs, genuinely fails with two deterministic failure codes ("expired", "path_unreachable"), and the CLI reports it via the real VIOLATION exit path (report.ok ? SUCCESS : EXIT_CODES.VIOLATION) rather than the happy path every prior scenario exercised. Exit 5 verified empirically 2026-08-19, stable over three runs — deterministic because both failure conditions are already true relative to any plausible CI clock (the registry entry expired in 2020) and the path is a fixed, guaranteed-absent literal, not a real filesystem probe of anything that could vary.

arbor serve fed a real MCP JSON-RPC session over stdin (initialize, notifications/initialized, then three tools/call requests) and closed with EOF — the same shutdown path bin.test.ts's and cli.test.ts's stdio-session tests already rely on, run here as a real child process instead of an in-process ArborMCPServer. Drives the arbor_query/arbor_command MCP tool boundary for two kinds nothing in the catalog had reached: agent.list (the whole @arbor agent catalog including zero live agents) and approval.request/approval.list (a full request-then-read roundtrip through RuntimeCatalogRouter.dispatchApprovalRequest and executeApprovalListQuery, including ApprovalService's real accept/lease-scope machinery). Exit 0 and all four JSON-RPC responses verified empirically 2026-08-19 (real invocation, three runs, stable; only the operation_id UUID varies run to run, which nothing here asserts on). count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same /proc-walking sandbox admission read as cli-serve-junior-tier-denied-mutation's note, verified empirically 2026-09-18.

arbor doctor --json against a scratch cwd pre-seeded with a real arbor.jsonc containing both `//` and `/* */` comments and a trailing comma before a closing brace. Every prior scenario ran doctor/config-consuming commands against a cwd with NO arbor.jsonc, so `loadConfig`'s `existsSync(configPath)` branch always took the `structuredClone(DEFAULT_CONFIG)` path and never called `loadConfigFromString`/`stripJsonc` at all (hollow_candidate, packages/arbor-config/src/loader.ts). This seeds the minimal real config file that forces the file-present branch. Exit 0 and `config_sources.file_present: true` verified empirically 2026-08-19.

arbor ledger repair --dir . --campaign <id> --reason ... --actor ... against a scratch cwd with no audit ledger at all for that campaign. `ledger-command.ts`'s repair branch refuses (CONFLICT) only when the ledger is BOTH `valid` AND its `tip_status` is something other than `sentinel_missing` — a wholly absent campaign ledger genuinely reports `{valid: true, tip_status: "sentinel_missing"}` (the same real state `production-ledger-verify-empty` already exercises for `verify`), so it is NOT refused and the sanctioned-repair path genuinely runs (verified by reading persist.ts's `classifyTipStatus`/`loadLedgerResult`, not assumed). `resolveGitHead` requires a real, discoverable git repository at `--dir`'s resolved path (it shells out to `git -C <dir> rev-parse HEAD`, which only needs HEAD to textually resolve to a SHA-shaped ref — verified empirically that git does not require the referenced commit object to actually exist) — the seeded `.git/HEAD`+`config`+`refs/heads/master`+`objects/` skeleton is the minimal plain-text git repository that satisfies it, entirely inside the hermetic scratch cwd. Closes a hollow_candidate: `performSanctionedRepair` (packages/arbor-audit/src/repair-log.ts) was production-reachable only through this one dispatch site (ledger-command.ts:310) and nothing in the prior catalog invoked it. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-19 (real invocation, three runs, stable; only `performed_at`/`content_hash` vary run to run, which nothing here asserts on).

arbor ledger verify --dir . --campaign <id> --json against a scratch cwd pre-seeded with a genuinely corrupted audit ledger: one real `gate_checkpoint` packet (captured verbatim from an actual `campaign.start` MCP dispatch against this same CLI, 2026-08-19) whose `content_hash` field has been hand-corrupted to an all-zero value that does not match the packet's real recomputed hash. `loadLedgerCore` (persist.ts) parses the JSON successfully, then `EvidenceLedger.verifyIntegrity()` detects the hash mismatch and the loader throws `AuditIntegrityError` — caught, quarantined, and surfaced as `diagnostics` — genuinely invoking the class nothing in the prior catalog constructed (hollow_candidate, packages/arbor-audit/src/audit.ts). This is corruption of one real field on a real record, not a hand-built ledger shape: the packet's structure, ids, and every other field are exactly what the production code path emits. Exit 5 (VIOLATION, since `valid: false`) verified empirically 2026-08-19, stable (no timestamps or ids here are regenerated at run time).

arbor serve fed a real MCP JSON-RPC session that creates a real campaign (`campaign.start`) and then drives three evidence-recording command kinds nothing in the prior catalog reached: `userinput.ask` (RuntimeCatalogRouter.dispatchUserInput -> manager.askForUserInput -> EvidenceLedger.recordRequestUserInput -> validateRequestUserInput), `userinput.answer` (-> manager.answerUserInput -> recordUserInputAnswer -> validateUserInputAnswer), and `compaction.record` (RuntimeCatalogRouter.dispatchCompactionRecord -> manager.recordCompactionLifecycle -> recordCompactionLifecycle -> validateCompactionLifecycle) — all three genuinely production-reachable MCP command kinds (`runtime-catalog.ts`'s own `RUNTIME_CATALOG`), matching exactly the payload shapes `liveness-runner.ts`'s own self-check trajectories already use for these same kinds. Closes three of the eleven hollow_candidate symbols in packages/arbor-audit/src/audit.ts. `record_id: "userinput_2"` is deterministic, not guessed: the ledger's id counter is a simple per-process sequence over every record kind, and this session always records exactly one prior packet (the campaign_start gate_checkpoint, `trace_1`) before the question is asked. Exit 0 and all four dispatches accepted verified empirically 2026-08-19 (real invocation, three runs, stable; only operation_id UUIDs and timestamps vary run to run, which nothing here asserts on). count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same /proc-walking sandbox admission read as cli-serve-junior-tier-denied-mutation's note, verified empirically 2026-09-18.

The same `arbor run --once --executor deterministic` shape as production-deterministic-campaign, but with `git_init: true` so the scratch cwd is a real one-commit git repository before the CLI is spawned. This is the scenario that closes the single highest-leverage gap in the catalog: `arbor run` always constructs a real `WorktreeManager` (demo.ts:709, ADR-001 isolation always on), whose `acquireLease` calls `git rev-parse HEAD` before `git worktree add` (worktree.ts). Against production-deterministic-campaign's non-git scratch cwd that HEAD lookup fails, `CampaignManager.expandNode` (manager.ts:550) sees `isolation.result === "fail"` and returns before `beginExpansion` (tree.ts) ever runs — the root cause the operator identified for the majority of `gate:vi-findings`' 63 red findings. With a real repo the isolation gate genuinely PASSES: `acquireLease` creates a real leased worktree under `.worktrees/`, `expandNode` reaches `beginExpansion`, and the deterministic executor carries the node through to `CampaignManager.recordResult`'s evidence gate and critic verdict — `checkEvidence` (arbor-gate/src/gate.ts) and `verifyNode` (arbor-core/src/tree.ts) both fire, verified empirically 2026-08-20 via a standalone coverage capture before this was added to the catalog (all three of beginExpansion/verifyNode/checkEvidence: 0 invocations in the prior catalog, nonzero here).

`arbor task <text> --json` against a scratch cwd with no native provider configured and `ARBOR_OPENCODE_BIN` pinned to a guaranteed-missing absolute path. The scenario drives task-composer submission and ADR-062 arbiter intake: the zero-cost classifier records a real governed `arbiter_decision`, then the unavailable planner fails closed. The hardened product no longer fabricates an actionable proposal through a heuristic fallback; it returns a durable failed draft with recovery guidance and conflict exit 1. This is an expected governed refusal, not a successful task run, and its provider precondition cannot vary with the host PATH. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same /proc-walking sandbox admission read as cli-serve-junior-tier-denied-mutation's note, verified empirically 2026-09-18.

`arbor audit show forensic-four --json` — the `arbor audit` verb the prior catalog never drove at all. Loads and renders one real audit template (`.claude/skills/forensic-four-*`-backed fan spec) through `audit-command.ts`'s `show` path: template lookup, fan-width/section/deliverable/tool projection, and stdout formatting. `--json` is accepted but this subcommand's real behavior (verified empirically) still renders the human-readable summary regardless — an existing quirk of `audit-command.ts`, not something this scenario asserts on; only exit code and invocation are load-bearing here. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-20, output is deterministic (template content is static, no timestamps or ids).

`arbor ledger audit <campaign-id> --dir . --json` — the `audit` action of `arbor ledger`, distinct from `ledger verify`/`ledger repair` (both already covered) and never previously reached. Drives `ledger-command.ts`'s audit path against a scratch cwd with no ledger file for the named campaign. The expectation CHANGED 2026-09-30: this used to expect 0 on the reasoning that an absent ledger is "a real, valid outcome (ledger_valid: true, empty findings) rather than an error". That reasoning is the absence-as-zero defect: a campaign holding no evidence records was never audited, and exit 0 asserted a verdict never obtained. It now exits 5 (VIOLATION) and the payload carries `measured: false` with `unmeasured_campaigns`, matching what the human path has always said — "nothing to audit — that is UNMEASURED, not clean". This scenario is the canary for that correction, so it must now assert the non-zero exit.

`arbor command list` — the `arbor command` verb the prior catalog never drove. Real invocation of `loadCommandCatalog` (cli.ts): builds a `CommandCatalog` from `~/.arbor/commands` and `<cwd>/.arbor/commands`, installs any locally-trusted plugin's registered commands, and prints its `list()`/`diagnostics()` projection. Against a scratch cwd with neither directory populated this legitimately returns an empty catalog with no diagnostics — still a real pass through `CommandCatalog.fromLocations` and `PluginRegistry.list()`, not a stub. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-20, output is deterministic (`{"commands":[],"diagnostics":[]}` with nothing on disk to discover).

`arbor liveness --json` — the `arbor liveness` verb the prior catalog never drove. Exercises every registered liveness seam and consumer (`liveness-runner.ts`'s self-check trajectories) against a scratch cwd, producing a real attestation report with a genuine mix of answered/refused/indeterminate seams (e.g. `governance.snapshot` refused with a real ENOENT on the scratch cwd's missing `decisions/` directory, `a2a.cards` refused as not configured) — real refusals from real absent state, not fabricated ones. `--json` is accepted but this command's real behavior (verified empirically) still renders the human-readable attestation text regardless, matching the same quirk noted on `audit show`; only exit code and invocation are load-bearing here. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-20 (the attestation timestamp is the only thing that varies run to run).

`arbor selfhost --dry-run` against a real LINKED git worktree — the `arbor selfhost` verb the prior catalog never drove at all, and structurally undrivable with a bare `git_init: true` repo: `evaluateTargetSafety` (selfhost.ts) refuses to target a repo's own PRIMARY checkout as a self-hosting safety boundary (`forbidden_primary_checkout`), and a fresh single-worktree repo IS its own primary checkout by construction — verified empirically (a plain `git_init` scratch repo targeting itself refuses with exactly that error). `git_linked_worktree: true` grows a genuine second, LINKED worktree of the same repo (`git worktree add`), and `--target linked-worktree` points selfhost at that non-primary checkout, which clears the guard for the real reason it exists — not by defeating the check, but by reproducing the actual distinction (primary vs. linked worktree) it is checking for. `--dry-run` composes the full campaign plan (worktree branch, campaign id, task, model config) and prints it without dispatching to a model, keeping this hermetic and network-free. `--run-id` pins the run identity so `campaign_id`/`worktree_branch` are deterministic rather than clock+random. Exit 0 verified empirically 2026-08-20.

T5.3 (2026-08-23 remediation) real-surface scenario, WA-10 pattern (packages/arbor-mcp/tests/cli.test.ts): arbor serve over real stdio with NO --trusted-client flag, so RuntimeCatalogRouter defaults to caller_tier junior (RuntimeRouterOptions.caller_tier's own doc comment). Drives a real session.identity.mutate command, which the router's authorized()/entitledActionClasses(caller_tier) check refuses at the capability-tier boundary, then a real session.identity.get query, which junior may still perform. This is the run_class:cli product-surface scenario hollow-parity.mjs item 2 watches: the denial must surface in outcomes.jsonl as a permission outcome, never a validation one - a caller_tier rejection and a malformed-input rejection are different Hollow-shape findings, and the ok:true envelope-level exit code (0) proves this scenario cannot be distinguished from a silent success without outcome-aware observation. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- sandbox-broker.ts's processRoot() walks /proc to count tasks owned by the operator's uid during sandbox admission; same real-host-process-count dependency as production-flight-director-lifecycle's note, verified empirically 2026-09-18. See vi-observe.mjs's count_semantics handling.

T5.3 (2026-08-23 remediation) real-surface scenario, same chord pattern as packages/arbor-mcp/tests/tui-keyboard-scrolling.test.ts (WA-25/WA-26): real raw-terminal bytes over the scenario's stdin pipe, written before EOF rather than only closing stdin immediately the way production-tui-headless-boot does. Backslash then 1 (the Campaigns chord in SCREEN_NAV), ESC [ 6 ~ (PageDown), ESC [ B (Down arrow / row selection), then R - driving the terminal input decoder, the Campaigns screen's paging/selection reducer path, and whatever R dispatches through executeAction, none of which production-tui-headless-boot's immediately-closed stdin ever reaches. This is the run_class:tui product-surface scenario hollow-parity.mjs item 2 watches for a validation-outcome finding. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same TUI background-timer wall-clock race, verified empirically 2026-09-18. See production-tui-headless-boot's note and vi-observe.mjs's count_semantics handling.

Starts the real repository-local Flight Director in an isolated Git repository, observes its authenticated transport/operator/controller composition, and shuts it down through the production SIGINT lifecycle. No HTTP request is declared because Flight uses an authenticated Unix-domain socket; the readiness probe exists to exercise and terminate a long-lived service under coverage without inventing a second transport. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- repo-flight-process.ts's children()/descendantOf() enumerate every PID under /proc on the host machine to find this process's real descendants; their invocation count is a direct function of how many processes exist on the machine running vi:observe at that instant -- genuine external-environment state, not a defect in this repository or its harness. Verified empirically 2026-09-18 (count varied 432/438/438 across 3 consecutive runs with zero source changes). See vi-observe.mjs's count_semantics handling.

T5.3 (2026-08-23 remediation) real-surface scenario: arbor webui 0 started as a real child process, its one-use operator URL exchanged for the opaque session cookie, then probed over real HTTP against its own ephemeral loopback port and shut down with SIGINT - the same interrupt-driven path a real operator Ctrl-C takes. Hits all 9 of ArborWebUIServer.handleRequest's route branches in one authenticated session: GET / (index), GET /api/campaigns (list, empty), POST /api/runtime/command (a real campaign.start, creating the fixture campaign every later request depends on), GET /api/campaigns/:id (snapshot), GET /api/campaigns/:id/kb, GET /api/campaigns/:id/interrupt, GET /api/campaigns/:id for an unknown id (a real 404, WA-22/WA-23's own regression target), GET /api/stream (a live SSE connection, read once then destroyed), and POST /api/runtime/query with deliberately malformed JSON (a real 400 from readJsonBody's parse guard, J6-20's regression target). This is the run_class:web product-surface scenario hollow-parity.mjs item 2 watches for a validation-outcome finding. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same /proc-walking sandbox admission read as cli-serve-junior-tier-denied-mutation's note, verified empirically 2026-09-18.

scenarios.description: Closes a hollow-candidate: `resetIntentTurn` (packages/arbor-core/src/intent-admission.ts) is reached only from `TaskComposer.admitIntent` (task-composer.ts) when a draft is retried by a process that already ran `admitIntent` for that same draft once before -- `intentAdmissionStates` is in-memory only (never persisted; see `TaskComposer.restore()`), so this genuinely requires two `taskcomposer.retry` dispatches inside the SAME `arbor serve` process, not two CLI invocations. `draft_id` is normally server-assigned (`draft-${randomUUID()}`), unknowable at authoring time and unusable in vi-observe's static stdin -- worked around by seeding a real-shaped `TaskComposerDraft` (status `failed`, revision 1) directly into `.arbor/task-composer/drafts.json` under a fixed id `TaskComposer.restore()` loads at boot, so retry's stable `draft_id` (only `revision` advances) is known ahead of time. `--trusted-client` is required: `taskcomposer.retry` needs the `senior` capability tier, refused for the default junior caller (verified empirically). First `taskcomposer.retry` (expected_revision 1) has no prior admission state in this fresh process, so `admitIntent` calls `createIntentAdmissionState` and fails again via `plan()`'s real opencode-spawn ENOENT (`ARBOR_OPENCODE_BIN` pinned missing, same trick as production-task-submit-heuristic-arbiter) -- revision advances 1->3 (`retry()`'s own "planning" update, then `plan()`'s "failed" update). Second `taskcomposer.retry` (expected_revision 3) now finds a prior admission state for this draft id in `intentAdmissionStates` and `admitIntent` calls `resetIntentTurn` instead -- verified empirically 2026-09-18 by a temporary debug probe against the compiled dist (not committed) confirming the exact call, and by three stable real runs of this scenario (revision sequence 1->3->5, both `taskcomposer.retry` dispatches `accepted:true`, exit 0). count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same /proc-walking sandbox admission read as cli-serve-junior-tier-denied-mutation's note, verified empirically 2026-09-18. CORRECTED 2026-10-06: the two retries were written to stdin in one burst, and `arbor serve` dispatches JSON-RPC requests concurrently, so the second `taskcomposer.retry` raced the first (observed: `expected 3, found 2` conflict, first call cancelled at EOF) and `resetIntentTurn` was never reached in a fresh run despite the earlier claim. `stdin_await_response` (vi-observe.mjs) now holds each JSON-RPC request line back until the server has answered the previous one, so retry 1 finishes (revision 1->3) before retry 2 arrives regardless of host load (a fixed gap was tried first and failed under load average 60), and `stdin_linger_ms` holds stdin open after the last response before EOF.

scenarios.description: Closes a hollow-candidate: `latestGateRefusal` (cli.ts) is called unconditionally inside `awaitConfirmedCampaign` once a task-composer confirm genuinely admits and awaits a real campaign -- reachable only past `taskcomposer.confirm`, a path no prior scenario reached (production-task-submit-heuristic-arbiter fails during `plan()`, before any campaign exists, so `awaitConfirmedCampaign` returns at its own early `draft.campaign_id === null` guard without ever calling `latestGateRefusal`). `--tier direct` (an operator-forced governance tier) bypasses the native planner entirely, so no provider/credentials are needed; the task text names a concrete file so `classifyAndRepairMutatingActions` can derive a `high_risk_tool_scope` and admission succeeds. With no `git_init` (the scratch cwd is not a git repository), `CampaignManager.expandNode`'s isolation gate genuinely fails on the root node (`WorktreeManager.acquireLease`'s `git rev-parse HEAD` has nothing to resolve) -- the same real isolation-gate mechanism production-deterministic-campaign and production-git-repo-real-agent-loop-campaign already exercise from the `arbor run` side, reached here from the task-composer side instead. The halted campaign's node carries a real, non-"pass" `gate_records` entry; `latestGateRefusal` finds it and the CLI's JSON `campaign_result.gate_refusal` is populated (`gate: "isolation"`, `code: "gate_isolation_fail"`) rather than null. Exit 3 and a non-null `gate_refusal` verified empirically 2026-09-18, stable over three runs. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same /proc-walking sandbox admission read as cli-serve-junior-tier-denied-mutation's note, verified empirically 2026-09-18.

scenarios.description: Closes a hollow-candidate: `shouldRefreshFocusedTree` (operator-campaign-focus.ts) has exactly one call site, inside `refreshExecutionStatus`, itself invoked ONLY by a 2000ms `setInterval` (`executionStatusTimer`) -- no eager call at boot. Every prior TUI scenario supplies static stdin that vi-observe's `spawnSync`-based process runner writes and closes essentially instantly (sub-second, verified empirically 2026-09-18), so the TUI's own `stdin.once("end", finish)` shutdown always won the race against this timer and the function was never invoked. This scenario uses the new `stdin_linger_ms` scenario field (vi-observe.mjs's `runLingeringStdinScenario`, added alongside this catalog widening): stdin is written immediately but held open for 4500ms of real wall-clock time -- long enough for the interval to fire at least once -- before EOF triggers the normal shutdown path, still one real spawned dist entry with the same coverage/outcome-sink wiring as every other scenario, no second transport. `refreshExecutionStatus` also needs a genuinely "active" campaign: `arbor tui`'s normal (non-`--resume`) launch hides every campaign that existed at boot from `displayCampaignId()` via `preexistingCampaignIds` (`options.resume === true ? new Set() : new Set(listCampaigns())`) -- so `--resume` and a seeded, real, previously-admitted campaign are both required, not optional. `seed_files` is a verbatim capture of the full `.arbor/` persistence tree (19 files) a real, credential-free `arbor task "create vi-observe-fixture.txt with the text hello" --tier direct --json` run produced against an isolated scratch cwd on 2026-09-18 -- a real halted campaign (`composer-draft-...`), not a hand-built fixture. Verified empirically: `shouldRefreshFocusedTree(campaignId, currentTree)` invoked with the seeded campaign's real id, stable over three runs. count_semantics: "presence_only" (2026-09-18 determinism remediation, worktree feat/observe-determinism) -- this scenario's downstream symbols (TUI render/query dispatch reached from the 2000ms executionStatusTimer, the 500ms haltWatchTimer, the 1000ms outputDetailTimer, and other independent setInterval timers in tui.ts) fire a real-time-dependent number of times inside the stdin_linger_ms window -- verified empirically over 3 consecutive full-catalog `vi:observe` runs and 5 isolated single-scenario runs on 2026-09-18: presence (was the symbol invoked at least once) was 100% stable across all 8 runs, but raw V8 invocation counts for timer-reached symbols varied by up to ~30% run to run (e.g. newestVisibleCampaignId: 20, 26, 26 across 3 runs) purely from OS scheduling jitter in how many timer ticks landed inside the real-wall-clock window. shouldRefreshFocusedTree itself (the symbol this scenario exists to close a hollow-candidate lead on) was stable at count 1 in every run. See vi-observe.mjs's count_semantics handling for what this clamps and why.

Closes a hollow-candidate: `createCanopyDebugJournal` (canopy-debug-journal.ts) is constructed only by `createCanopyDebugCaptureStore` (canopy-debug-capture.ts:137), and `runTui` creates that store only when `isCanopyDebugEnabled()` (canopy-debug-launch.ts) sees `CANOPY_DEBUG_ENABLED=1` -- the switch the dedicated canopy-debug launcher sets. No prior scenario set it, so the whole capture path (the SQLite journal, `capture-index.jsonl`, the launch-scoped `session_open`/`token_usage` events and the adapter telemetry sink) was wired but never run. This is the same `arbor tui --renderer stdout` entry as production-tui-headless-boot with that one environment variable added, stdin closed immediately so the TUI's own stdin-EOF shutdown closes the journal cleanly (exit 0). The journal lands under the scenario's scratch cwd (`.arbor/canopy-debug/`, `defaultCanopyDebugPersistenceDir`'s project-local fallback), never outside it. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same TUI background-timer wall-clock race as production-tui-headless-boot.

Closes a hollow-candidate: `GitWorkspaceService`, `GovernedWorktreeOperations`, `GitProjectionWatcher` and `gitWorkspaceIdentity` (git-workspace-projection.ts) are constructed only by createCliRuntime (cli.ts) inside a `try { new GitAdapter(cwd) }` that silently falls through when `cwd` is not a git repository -- and every prior TUI/serve scenario ran in a bare scratch directory, so `GitAdapter` threw (`GitAdapterError` is observed) and the service was never built. `git_init: true` gives the scratch cwd a real repository (see `gitInitScratchRepo`), so the adapter constructs, the service is registered as the `git-projection-watcher` runtime lifecycle component (cli.ts), `GitWorkspaceService.start()` opens a `GitProjectionWatcher` (fs watchers plus the status poll), and `watch()`'s own debounced `schedule()` (100ms) takes a `GitAdapter.snapshot()`, which lists the worktrees and derives every id through `gitWorkspaceIdentity` -- a timer the TUI's stdin-EOF shutdown would otherwise tear down first, so stdin is held open for `stdin_linger_ms` (6000, sized for TUI boot under host load) before EOF, the same device as production-tui-resume-execution-status-poll. Same `arbor tui --renderer stdout` entry as production-tui-headless-boot; EOF then triggers the clean exit 0, which also calls the service's `close()`. count_semantics: "presence_only" -- same TUI background-timer wall-clock race as production-tui-headless-boot.
